items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: Of the ones that I’ve met, the one that I am most fond of is Johnny Mercer. I met him by accident... I became friendly with a bunch at Eddie Condon’s place.

ctx.x: Who were some of your big favorites in the 30’s?

I knew more favorites than individuals. I suppose that Coon Sanders, I loved to hear them play. McKinney’s Cotton Pickers was a jazz band. There’s a new one now in Detroit but this was the old one. I just knew the name, I never saw them. “It’s Tight Like That” was a © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-

jazz tune and “Rosetta” and numbers like that. And that was McKinney’s Cotton Pickers, not Coon Sanders. The Coon Sanders, they had a tune called “Deep Henderson” I’d never heard before, and I think there’s: Flamin’ mamie/The sure fire vamp/The hottest baby in town/She’s a heart scorcher/She loves torture/She loves to burn ‘em down.
